Setup

Load CSIRO colour palette and required packages for spatial data, data manipulation, and plot composition.

source("code/CSIRO_colours.R")

library(sf)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)

Load Data

Import the deduplicated and full (with repeat tests) datasets, filtered to 2014-2024.

data_no_multi <- read.csv("data/preprocessed_with_SA_info_no_multi.csv") %>%
  filter(YOT >= 2014 & YOT <= 2024)

data_with_multi <- read.csv("data/preprocessed_with_SA_info.csv") %>%
  filter(YOT >= 2014 & YOT <= 2024)

Annual Testing Summaries

Calculate yearly totals of tests performed, positive results, and positivity rates for both unique patient and all-test perspectives.

Unique Patients

# Summarise data_no_multi
pos_annual_prop_no_multi <- data_no_multi %>%
  group_by(YOT) %>%
  summarise(
    total_tests = n(),
    positive_tests = sum(Status == "Positive", na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  mutate(pos_prop = (positive_tests / total_tests) * 100) %>%
  mutate(pos_prop = round(pos_prop, 2)) %>%
  rename(Year = YOT) %>%
  # Remove early testing years and 2025 which is an incomplete year
  filter(
    Year != 2012,
    Year != 2013,
    Year != 2025
  )

cat("=== SUMMARY TABLE UNIQUE PATIENTS ===\n")
print(pos_annual_prop_no_multi)

Compound Annual Growth Rates (CAGR)

Quantify the rate of growth in testing volume, positive case numbers, and positivity rate over defined time periods using log-linear regression with 95% confidence intervals.

Year-over-Year Change (Unique Patients)

Calculate year-over-year absolute and percentage change in positive case numbers.

positive_tests_trend_no_multi <- pos_annual_prop_no_multi %>%
  filter(Year >= 2014, Year <= 2024) %>%
  arrange(Year) %>%
  mutate(
    # Calculate year-over-year percentage change in positive tests
    yoy_change = (positive_tests - lag(positive_tests)) /
      lag(positive_tests) *
      100,
    yoy_change = round(yoy_change, 2)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Year, positive_tests, total_tests, pos_prop, yoy_change)
positive_tests_trend_with_multi <- pos_annual_prop_multi %>%
  filter(Year >= 2014, Year <= 2024) %>%
  arrange(Year) %>%
  mutate(
    # Calculate year-over-year percentage change in positive tests
    yoy_change = (positive_tests - lag(positive_tests)) /
      lag(positive_tests) *
      100,
    yoy_change = round(yoy_change, 2)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Year, positive_tests, total_tests, pos_prop, yoy_change)
library(boot)

calculate_cagr_with_ci <- function(data, value_col, start_year, end_year) {
  # Filter data for period
  period_data <- data %>%
    filter(Year >= start_year, Year <= end_year)

  # Fit log-linear model
  model <- lm(log(get(value_col)) ~ Year, data = period_data)

  # Extract coefficients
  coef_year <- coef(model)["Year"]
  se_year <- summary(model)$coefficients["Year", "Std. Error"]

  # Calculate CAGR and CI
  cagr <- (exp(coef_year) - 1) * 100
  cagr_lower <- (exp(coef_year - 1.96 * se_year) - 1) * 100
  cagr_upper <- (exp(coef_year + 1.96 * se_year) - 1) * 100

  return(list(
    cagr = cagr,
    ci_lower = cagr_lower,
    ci_upper = cagr_upper,
    se = se_year,
    model = model
  ))
}

Testing Volume CAGR

Estimate compound annual growth rates for testing volume across pre- and post-2021 periods.

test_2014_2021 <- calculate_cagr_with_ci(
  positive_tests_trend_no_multi,
  "total_tests",

  2021
)

)

Segmented Regression Analysis

Fit piecewise linear regression models to identify structural breakpoints in testing trends, with a fixed breakpoint at 2020 for positive cases.

library(segmented)

time_model_pos <- lm(positive_tests ~ Year, data = pos_annual_prop_no_multi)

# Your segmented model with fixed breakpoint at 2020
segmented_model_pos <- segmented(
  time_model_pos,
  seg.Z = ~Year,
  psi = 2020,
  control = seg.control(it.max = 0)
)

cat("=== BREAKPOINT ANALYSIS (Fixed at 2020) ===\n")
summary(segmented_model_pos)

# MANUALLY EXTRACT SLOPES from coefficients
coefs <- coef(segmented_model_pos)
coef_summary <- summary(segmented_model_pos)$coefficients

# First segment slope (before 2020)
slope_before <- coefs["Year"]
se_before <- coef_summary["Year", "Std. Error"]

# Second segment slope (after 2020)
# Total slope after breakpoint = Year + U1.Year
slope_after <- coefs["Year"] + coefs["U1.Year"]
# SE for sum of coefficients (using variance formula)
var_after <- coef_summary["Year", "Std. Error"]^2 +
  coef_summary["U1.Year", "Std. Error"]^2 +
  2 * vcov(segmented_model_pos)["Year", "U1.Year"]
se_after <- sqrt(var_after)

cat("\n=== SEGMENT SLOPES ===\n")
cat(
  "First segment (2014-2020):",
  round(slope_before, 2),
  "±",
  round(se_before, 2),
  "cases/year\n"
)
cat(
  "Second segment (2020-2024):",
  round(slope_after, 2),
  "±",
  round(se_after, 2),
  "cases/year\n"
)
cat("Acceleration factor:", round(slope_after / slope_before, 2), "×\n")

# Calculate R² for the first segment (2014-2020)
first_segment_data <- pos_annual_prop_no_multi %>%
  filter(Year <= 2020)

first_segment_model <- lm(positive_tests ~ Year, data = first_segment_data)

cat("\n=== FIRST SEGMENT (2014-2020) ===\n")
cat("Slope:", round(coef(first_segment_model)["Year"], 2), "cases/year\n")
cat(
  "SE:",
  round(summary(first_segment_model)$coefficients["Year", "Std. Error"], 2),
  "\n"
)
cat("R²:", round(summary(first_segment_model)$r.squared, 4), "\n")
cat("Adjusted R²:", round(summary(first_segment_model)$adj.r.squared, 4), "\n")
cat(
  "p-value:",
  format.pval(
    summary(first_segment_model)$coefficients["Year", "Pr(>|t|)"],
    digits = 4
  ),
  "\n"
)

# Calculate R² for the second segment (2021-2024)
second_segment_data <- pos_annual_prop_no_multi %>%
  filter(Year > 2020)

second_segment_model <- lm(positive_tests ~ Year, data = second_segment_data)

cat("\n=== SECOND SEGMENT (2021-2024) ===\n")
cat("Slope:", round(coef(second_segment_model)["Year"], 2), "cases/year\n")
cat(
  "SE:",
  round(summary(second_segment_model)$coefficients["Year", "Std. Error"], 2),
  "\n"
)
cat("R²:", round(summary(second_segment_model)$r.squared, 4), "\n")
cat("Adjusted R²:", round(summary(second_segment_model)$adj.r.squared, 4), "\n")
cat(
  "p-value:",
  format.pval(
    summary(second_segment_model)$coefficients["Year", "Pr(>|t|)"],
    digits = 4
  ),
  "\n"
)

# Overall segmented model R²
cat("\n=== OVERALL SEGMENTED MODEL ===\n")
cat("R²:", round(summary(segmented_model_pos)$r.squared, 4), "\n")
cat("Adjusted R²:", round(summary(segmented_model_pos)$adj.r.squared, 4), "\n")
cat("AIC:", round(AIC(segmented_model_pos), 2), "\n")

# Compare with simple linear model (no breakpoint)
simple_model <- lm(positive_tests ~ Year, data = pos_annual_prop_no_multi)
cat("\n=== COMPARISON: Simple Linear Model ===\n")
cat("R²:", round(summary(simple_model)$r.squared, 4), "\n")
cat("AIC:", round(AIC(simple_model), 2), "\n")
cat(
  "AIC improvement with breakpoint:",
  round(AIC(simple_model) - AIC(segmented_model_pos), 2),
  "\n"
)

positive_tests_trend_no_multi <- pos_annual_prop_no_multi %>%
  filter(Year >= 2014, Year <= 2024) %>%
  arrange(Year) %>%
  mutate(
    # Calculate year-over-year absolute change
    yoy_absolute_change = positive_tests - lag(positive_tests),
    # Calculate year-over-year percentage change in positive tests
    yoy_change = (positive_tests - lag(positive_tests)) /
      lag(positive_tests) *
      100,
    yoy_change = round(yoy_change, 2)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Year,
    positive_tests,
    yoy_absolute_change,
    yoy_change,
    total_tests,
    pos_prop
  )

Year-over-Year Change Summary

Calculate and compare mean year-over-year absolute changes in positive case numbers between the pre-2020 and post-2020 periods.

# Calculate mean YoY absolute change for 2014-2020 period
mean_yoy_2014_2020 <- positive_tests_trend_no_multi %>%
  filter(Year >= 2014, Year <= 2020) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_yoy_absolute = mean(yoy_absolute_change, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_yoy_absolute = median(yoy_absolute_change, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_yoy_absolute = sd(yoy_absolute_change, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_years = sum(!is.na(yoy_absolute_change))
  )

cat("=== MEAN YEAR-OVER-YEAR CHANGE (2014-2020) ===\n")

Total Tests Breakpoint

Fit a segmented regression to total test counts with an automatically estimated breakpoint to identify when testing volume acceleration occurred.

# Test for structural breaks in the time series
time_model_tests <- lm(total_tests ~ Year, data = pos_annual_prop_no_multi)
segmented_model_tests <- segmented(time_model_tests, seg.Z = ~Year, npsi = 1)

cat("=== BREAKPOINT ANALYSIS ===\n")
print(summary(segmented_model_tests))
print(segmented_model_tests$psi)

# Plot with breakpoint
breakpoint_year <- round(segmented_model_tests$psi[2])
cat("Estimated breakpoint year:", breakpoint_year, "\n")

Multiple R-squared:  0.7152,    Adjusted R-squared:  0.644 
F-statistic: 10.04 on 1 and 4 DF,  p-value: 0.03388
# Extract slopes from segmented model
coefs <- coef(segmented_model_PR)

# Second segment slope (after 2019 breakpoint)
# Total slope after breakpoint = Year + U1.Year
slope_after_2019 <- coefs["Year"] + coefs["U1.Year"]

cat("=== SECOND SEGMENT (2019-2024) POSITIVITY RATE ===\n")
cat("Slope:", round(slope_after_2019, 3), "% per year\n")

# Calculate standard error for second segment slope
coef_summary <- summary(segmented_model_PR)$coefficients
var_after <- coef_summary["Year", "Std. Error"]^2 +
  coef_summary["U1.Year", "Std. Error"]^2 +
  2 * vcov(segmented_model_PR)["Year", "U1.Year"]
se_after <- sqrt(var_after)
cat("SE:", round(se_after, 3), "\n")

# Calculate R² for the second segment (2019-2024)
second_segment_PR <- pos_annual_prop_no_multi %>%
  filter(Year >= 2019, Year <= 2024)

second_segment_PR_model <- lm(pos_prop ~ Year, data = second_segment_PR)

cat("R²:", round(summary(second_segment_PR_model)$r.squared, 4), "\n")
cat(
  "Adjusted R²:",
  round(summary(second_segment_PR_model)$adj.r.squared, 4),
  "\n"
)
cat(
  "p-value:",
  format.pval(
    summary(second_segment_PR_model)$coefficients["Year", "Pr(>|t|)"],
    digits = 4
  ),
  "\n"
)

# Show full summary
cat("\n=== FULL REGRESSION DETAILS ===\n")
summary(second_segment_PR_model)

Trend Plots

Generate a three-panel figure showing annual trends in total tests, positive case numbers, and positivity rates, each with segmented regression overlays and breakpoint indicators.

Plot Setup

Configure the plot theme and colour constants for the trend panels.

theme_set(
  theme_classic() +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(
        colour = "grey60",
        linewidth = 0.1
      ),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 11),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.title.x = element_blank(),
      axis.line = element_line(colour = "grey60"),
      axis.ticks = element_line(colour = "grey60"),
      text = element_text(family = "Arial")
    )
)

TOTAL_TESTS_COL <- "#999999"
POS_TESTS_COL <- "grey10"
RATE_COL <- "grey10"

Panel A: Total Tests

Bar chart of annual total alpha-gal sIgE tests with segmented regression overlay and confidence band.

# Plot 1: Total tests bar chart

# Extract fitted values and confidence intervals from segmented model
fitted_data <- data.frame(
  Year = pos_annual_prop_no_multi$Year,
  fitted = fitted(segmented_model_tests),
  residuals = residuals(segmented_model_tests)
)

# Calculate standard errors for confidence intervals
# Get predictions with standard errors
pred_se <- predict(segmented_model_tests, se.fit = TRUE)
fitted_data$se <- pred_se$se.fit
fitted_data$lower <- fitted_data$fitted - 1.96 * fitted_data$se
fitted_data$upper <- fitted_data$fitted + 1.96 * fitted_data$se

# Get breakpoint location
breakpoint_year <- segmented_model_tests$psi[2]

# Create plot with segmented regression overlay
p1 <- ggplot(pos_annual_prop_multi, aes(x = Year)) +
  # Bar chart
  geom_col(
    aes(y = total_tests),
    alpha = 0.7,
    fill = TOTAL_TESTS_COL,
    width = 0.9
  ) +
  # Add confidence interval ribbon
  geom_ribbon(
    data = fitted_data,
    aes(y = fitted, ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
    fill = "red",
    alpha = 0.15
  ) +
  # Add segmented regression line
  geom_line(
    data = fitted_data,
    aes(y = fitted),
    color = "red",
    size = 0.5,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  # Add vertical line at breakpoint
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 2022,
    linetype = "twodash",
    color = "black",
    alpha = 0.5,
    size = 0.8
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = expression("Total " * alpha * "-gal sIgE Tests"),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2014, 2024, 2)) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

Panel B: Positive Cases

Line plot of annual suspected MMA case counts with segmented regression overlay and breakpoint at 2020.

fitted_data$upper <- fitted_data$fitted + 1.96 * fitted_data$se

Testing Volume Decomposition

Decompose the growth in positive case numbers into contributions from changes in testing volume versus changes in positivity rate using counterfactual scenarios.

Counterfactual Scenarios

Model three counterfactual scenarios against a 2018-2020 baseline: fixing testing volume, fixing positivity rate, or fixing both, to isolate the drivers of increasing case numbers.

annual <- data_no_multi |>
  group_by(Year = YOT) |>
  summarise(
    total_tests = n(),
    positive = sum(Status == "Positive", na.rm = TRUE),
    negative = total_tests - positive,
    positivity_rate = positive / total_tests,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

annual |>
  mutate(
    positivity_pct = round(positivity_rate * 100, 2),
    yoy_tests_pct = round(
      (total_tests / lag(total_tests) - 1) * 100,
      1
    ),
    yoy_cases_pct = round(
      (positive / lag(positive) - 1) * 100,
      1
    )
  )

10  2023        1934      700     1234           0.362           36.2
11  2024        2155      787     1368           0.365           36.5
# ℹ 2 more variables: yoy_tests_pct <dbl>, yoy_cases_pct <dbl>
# Use pooled 2018-2020 as baseline (stable period before post-2020 expansion)
baseline_years <- 2018:2020
baseline <- annual |>
  filter(Year %in% baseline_years) |>
  summarise(
    total_tests = mean(total_tests),
    positive = mean(positive),
    negative = mean(negative),
    positivity_rate = sum(positive) / sum(total_tests) # pooled rate
  )
baseline_label <- "2018\u20132020"

counterfactual <- annual |>
  mutate(
    # Scenario 1: Testing volume fixed at baseline levels
    cf_fixed_volume = baseline$total_tests * positivity_rate,

    # Scenario 2: Positivity rate fixed at baseline level
    cf_fixed_rate = total_tests * baseline$positivity_rate,

    # Scenario 3: Both fixed (baseline cases)
    cf_both_fixed = baseline$positive
  )

p_counterfactual <- ggplot(counterfactual, aes(x = Year)) +
  # # Shaded region for counterfactual period
  # annotate(
  #   "rect",
  #   xmin = 2020,
  #   xmax = 2024,
  #   ymin = -Inf,
  #   ymax = Inf,
  #   fill = "lightblue",
  #   alpha = 0.3
  # ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = positive, colour = "Observed"),
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_point(aes(y = positive, colour = "Observed"), size = 2.5) +
  geom_line(
    aes(
      y = cf_fixed_rate,
      colour = paste0("Positivity rate fixed at ", baseline_label)
    ),
    linewidth = 0.6,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(
      y = cf_fixed_volume,
      colour = paste0("Testing volume fixed at ", baseline_label)
    ),
    linewidth = 0.6,
    linetype = "dotted"
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = setNames(
      c("grey10", "grey20", "grey30"),
      c(
        "Observed",
        paste0("Positivity rate fixed at ", baseline_label),
        paste0("Testing volume fixed at ", baseline_label)
      )
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2020:2024) +
  xlim(c(2020, 2024)) +
  ylim(c(300, 800)) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of suspected MMA cases",
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.direction = "vertical",
    legend.position = c(0.98, 0.06),
    legend.justification = c("right", "bottom"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9, family = "Ariel"),
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.key.width = unit(1, "cm"), # Add this line - width of rectangle
    legend.key.height = unit(0.4, "cm"), # Add this line - height of rectangle
    legend.box.background = element_rect(
      fill = "white",
      color = "grey70",
      linewidth = 0.5
    ),
    legend.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2)
  )

p_counterfactual
ggsave(
  "plots/Final_Plots/Fig_S3_counterfactual_scenarios.png",
  p_counterfactual,
  width = 20,
  height = 14,
  units = "cm",
  bg = "white"
)

Geographic Expansion vs Testing Intensity

Decompose testing volume growth into contributions from geographic expansion (more SA3 regions testing) versus increased testing intensity (more tests per region).

# Number of unique SA3 regions testing per year
sa3_expansion <- data_no_multi %>%
  group_by(YOT) %>%
  summarise(
    n_sa3_regions = n_distinct(SA3_code),
    n_tests = n(),
    tests_per_region = n_tests / n_sa3_regions
  )

sa3_expansion

# Analyze geographic expansion alongside case growth
geographic_expansion_analysis <- sa3_expansion %>%
  left_join(pos_annual_prop_no_multi, by = c("YOT" = "Year")) %>%
  mutate(
    regions_expansion_pct = (n_sa3_regions / first(n_sa3_regions) - 1) * 100,
    tests_expansion_pct = (n_tests / first(n_tests) - 1) * 100,
    intensity_expansion_pct = (tests_per_region / first(tests_per_region) - 1) *
      100,
    cases_expansion_pct = (positive_tests / first(positive_tests) - 1) * 100
  )

# Test correlation between geographic expansion and cases
cor_regions_cases <- cor.test(
  sa3_expansion$n_sa3_regions,
  pos_annual_prop_no_multi$positive_tests
)

cor_intensity_cases <- cor.test(
  sa3_expansion$tests_per_region,
  pos_annual_prop_no_multi$positive_tests
)

  "\n"
)

  ),
  "(",

      sa3_expansion$tests_per_region[1] -
      1) *
      100,
    1
  ),
  "%)\n\n"
)

cat("Correlation: Geographic reach vs Cases\n")
print(cor_regions_cases)
cat("\nCorrelation: Testing intensity vs Cases\n")
print(cor_intensity_cases)

# Decompose testing growth into geographic vs intensity components
decomposition <- sa3_expansion %>%
  mutate(
    total_tests_predicted = n_sa3_regions[1] * tests_per_region, # If only intensity changed
    total_tests_geographic = n_sa3_regions * tests_per_region[1], # If only reach changed
    geographic_effect = (total_tests_geographic / n_tests[1] - 1) * 100,
    intensity_effect = (total_tests_predicted / n_tests[1] - 1) * 100
  )

cat("\n=== DECOMPOSITION OF TESTING GROWTH ===\n")
print(
  decomposition %>%
    dplyr::select(
      YOT,
      n_sa3_regions,
      tests_per_region,
      geographic_effect,
      intensity_effect
    )
)

theme_set(

# Calculate mean and SE of tests per region across SA3s within each year
sa3_expansion_with_se <- data_no_multi %>%
  group_by(YOT, SA3_code) %>%
  summarise(n_tests = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(YOT) %>%
  summarise(
    n_sa3_regions = n_distinct(SA3_code),
    mean_tests_per_region = mean(n_tests),
    sd_tests = sd(n_tests),
    se_tests = sd(n_tests) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
# PLOT 1
# Fit model for geographic expansion
geo_model <- lm(n_sa3_regions ~ YOT, data = sa3_expansion)

# Get predictions with confidence intervals
geo_predictions <- data.frame(
  YOT = sa3_expansion$YOT,
  fit = predict(geo_model, se.fit = TRUE)$fit,
  se = predict(geo_model, se.fit = TRUE)$se.fit
) %>%
  mutate(
    lower = fit - 1.96 * se,
    upper = fit + 1.96 * se
  )

# Plot with confidence band

  sa3_expansion,
  aes(x = YOT, y = n_sa3_regions)
) +
  geom_ribbon(

    aes(y = fit, ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
    fill = "grey70",
    alpha = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_line(color = "black", size = 0.8) +
  geom_point(color = "black", size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2014, 2024, 2)) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Number of SA3 regions",
    #title = "Geographic Expansion with 95% CI"
  )
# PLOT 2

# MULTIPLICATIVE INTERACTION FOR POSITIVE CASES
# ============================================================

# Get positive cases for 2014 and 2024
positive_2014 <- pos_annual_prop_no_multi %>%
  filter(Year == 2014) %>%
  pull(positive_tests)

positive_2024 <- pos_annual_prop_no_multi %>%
  filter(Year == 2024) %>%
  pull(positive_tests)

cat("=== MULTIPLICATIVE INTERACTION ANALYSIS (POSITIVE CASES) ===\n\n")

# Actual increase in positive cases
actual_pos_increase <- positive_2024 - positive_2014
actual_pos_pct <- (actual_pos_increase / positive_2014) * 100

cat("Actual positive cases:\n")
cat("  2014:", positive_2014, "cases\n")
cat("  2024:", positive_2024, "cases\n")
cat("  Absolute increase:", actual_pos_increase, "cases\n")
cat("  Percentage increase:", round(actual_pos_pct, 1), "%\n\n")

# Calculate what positive cases would be under each isolation scenario
# Assume positivity rate stays constant at ~33%
baseline_positivity <- 0.33 # Average positivity rate

# Scenario 1: Geographic expansion only effect on cases
# If only geography expanded: geographic_only_tests * positivity rate
geographic_only_cases <- geographic_only_tests * baseline_positivity

# Scenario 2: Intensity only effect on cases
# If only intensity increased: intensity_only_tests * positivity rate
intensity_only_cases <- intensity_only_tests * baseline_positivity

# Baseline positive cases if maintained
baseline_cases_2014 <- positive_2014

# Individual contributions (relative to baseline)
geographic_contribution_cases <- geographic_only_cases - baseline_cases_2014
intensity_contribution_cases <- intensity_only_cases - baseline_cases_2014
additive_total_cases <- geographic_contribution_cases +
  intensity_contribution_cases

cat("If effects were additive (assuming constant 33% positivity):\n")
cat(
  "  Geographic contribution:",
  round(geographic_contribution_cases, 0),
  "cases\n"
)
cat(
  "  Intensity contribution:",
  round(intensity_contribution_cases, 0),
  "cases\n"
)
cat("  Sum:", round(additive_total_cases, 0), "cases\n")
cat(
  "  Expected total (baseline + sum):",
  round(baseline_cases_2014 + additive_total_cases, 0),
  "cases\n\n"
)

# Interaction effect for positive cases
interaction_effect_cases <- actual_pos_increase - additive_total_cases
interaction_pct_cases <- (interaction_effect_cases / actual_pos_increase) * 100

cat("Multiplicative interaction (positive cases):\n")
cat("  Actual increase:", actual_pos_increase, "cases\n")
cat("  Additive prediction:", round(additive_total_cases, 0), "cases\n")
cat("  Interaction effect:", round(interaction_effect_cases, 0), "cases\n")
cat(
  "  Interaction as % of total growth:",
  round(interaction_pct_cases, 1),
  "%\n\n"
)

# Test interaction using regression on positive cases
# Model positive cases as function of regions, intensity, and their interaction
cases_by_year <- pos_annual_prop_no_multi %>%
  left_join(sa3_expansion, by = c("Year" = "YOT"))

interaction_model_cases <- lm(
  positive_tests ~ n_sa3_regions * tests_per_region,
  data = cases_by_year
)

cat("=== INTERACTION MODEL (POSITIVE CASES) ===\n")
summary(interaction_model_cases)

# Extract interaction p-value
interaction_p_cases <- summary(interaction_model_cases)$coefficients[
  "n_sa3_regions:tests_per_region",
  "Pr(>|t|)"
]

cat(
  "\nInteraction term p-value:",
  format.pval(interaction_p_cases, digits = 4),
  "\n"
)

cat("\n=== FINAL STATEMENT (POSITIVE CASES) ===\n")
cat(
  "The observed total increase of",
  round(actual_pos_pct, 0),
  "% (",
  actual_pos_increase,
  " cases) demonstrates a multiplicative rather than\n"
)
cat(
  "additive effect, with the interaction between geographic expansion and regional\n"
)
cat(
  "intensification accounting for",
  round(interaction_pct_cases, 1),
  "% of the total growth (",
  round(interaction_effect_cases, 0),
  " cases, p ",
  ifelse(
    interaction_p_cases < 0.001,
    "< 0.001",
    paste("=", round(interaction_p_cases, 3))
  ),
  ").\n"
)

# Compare observed growth to what would happen under additive model
decomposition_test <- sa3_expansion %>%
  filter(YOT %in% c(2014, 2024)) %>%
  summarise(
    regions_2014 = first(n_sa3_regions),
    regions_2024 = last(n_sa3_regions),
    intensity_2014 = first(tests_per_region),
    intensity_2024 = last(tests_per_region),
    tests_2014 = first(n_tests),
    tests_2024 = last(n_tests),

    # Observed increase
    observed_increase = (tests_2024 - tests_2014) / tests_2014 * 100,

    # Expected under additive model
    geographic_only = (regions_2024 - regions_2014) * intensity_2014,
    intensity_only = (intensity_2024 - intensity_2014) * regions_2014,
    additive_expected = tests_2014 + geographic_only + intensity_only,
    additive_increase = (additive_expected - tests_2014) / tests_2014 * 100,

    # Expected under multiplicative model
    multiplicative_expected = regions_2024 * intensity_2024,
    multiplicative_increase = (multiplicative_expected - tests_2014) /
      tests_2014 *
      100,

    # Which model fits better?
    observed_vs_additive_diff = abs(tests_2024 - additive_expected),
    observed_vs_mult_diff = abs(tests_2024 - multiplicative_expected)
  )

cat("=== ADDITIVE vs MULTIPLICATIVE MODEL COMPARISON ===\n")
print(decomposition_test)

Testing intensity heterogeneity

# Calculate change in testing intensity for each SA3 region
# Need to get first and last year of testing for each region

sa3_intensity_change <- data_no_multi %>%
  group_by(SA3_code) %>%
  summarise(
    first_year = min(YOT),
    last_year = max(YOT),
    n_tests_first = sum(YOT == first_year),
    n_tests_last = sum(YOT == last_year),
    years_testing = n_distinct(YOT),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Calculate intensity change
  mutate(
    intensity_change = n_tests_last - n_tests_first,
    intensity_pct_change = ifelse(
      n_tests_first > 0,
      (intensity_change / n_tests_first) * 100,
      NA
    )
  ) %>%
  # Filter to regions testing in multiple years
  filter(years_testing >= 2, !is.na(intensity_pct_change))

cat("=== TESTING INTENSITY HETEROGENEITY ===\n\n")

# Summary statistics
intensity_summary <- sa3_intensity_change %>%
  summarise(
    n_regions = n(),
    median_change = median(intensity_pct_change, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_change = mean(intensity_pct_change, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_change = sd(intensity_pct_change, na.rm = TRUE),
    q25 = quantile(intensity_pct_change, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q75 = quantile(intensity_pct_change, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr = IQR(intensity_pct_change, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_change = min(intensity_pct_change, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_change = max(intensity_pct_change, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

print(intensity_summary)

cat(
  "\nMedian intensity change:",
  round(intensity_summary$median_change, 1),
  "%\n"
)
cat(
  "IQR:",
  round(intensity_summary$q25, 1),
  "% to",
  round(intensity_summary$q75, 1),
  "% (range:",
  round(intensity_summary$iqr, 1),
  "%)\n\n"
)

# Test for heterogeneity using coefficient of variation
cv <- (intensity_summary$sd_change / abs(intensity_summary$mean_change)) * 100
cat("Coefficient of Variation:", round(cv, 1), "%\n")
cat("(CV > 30% indicates high heterogeneity)\n\n")

# Statistical test: Levene's test for homogeneity of variance
# Compare variance across different testing eras
sa3_intensity_by_era <- sa3_intensity_change %>%
  mutate(
    testing_era = case_when(
      first_year <= 2016 ~ "Early",
      first_year <= 2019 ~ "Pre-COVID",
      first_year <= 2021 ~ "COVID",
      TRUE ~ "Recent"
    )
  )

# Levene's test
library(car)
levene_test <- leveneTest(
  intensity_pct_change ~ as.factor(testing_era),
  data = sa3_intensity_by_era
)

cat("=== LEVENE'S TEST (Homogeneity of Variance) ===\n")
print(levene_test)
cat(
  "\nInterpretation: p",
  ifelse(
    levene_test$`Pr(>F)`[1] < 0.001,
    "< 0.001",
    paste("=", round(levene_test$`Pr(>F)`[1], 3))
  ),
  ifelse(
    levene_test$`Pr(>F)`[1] < 0.05,
    " - Significant heterogeneity detected",
    " - No significant heterogeneity"
  ),
  "\n\n"
)

# Kruskal-Wallis test: Are intensity changes different across eras?
kruskal_test <- kruskal.test(
  intensity_pct_change ~ testing_era,
  data = sa3_intensity_by_era
)

cat("=== KRUSKAL-WALLIS TEST (Regional Differences) ===\n")
print(kruskal_test)
cat(
  "\nInterpretation: p",
  ifelse(
    kruskal_test$p.value < 0.001,
    "< 0.001",
    paste("=", round(kruskal_test$p.value, 3))
  ),
  ifelse(
    kruskal_test$p.value < 0.05,
    " - Significant differences across regions",
    " - No significant differences"
  ),
  "\n\n"
)


cat("=== FOR YOUR STATEMENT ===\n")
cat(
  "However, this intensification showed considerable heterogeneity across regions,\n"
)
cat(
  "with the median increase being",
  round(intensity_summary$median_change, 1),
  "% and interquartile range of\n"
)
cat(
  round(intensity_summary$q25, 1),
  "% to",
  round(intensity_summary$q75, 1),
  "% (IQR = ",
  round(intensity_summary$iqr, 1),
  "%, CV = ",
  round(cv, 1),
  "%, Levene's test p ",
  ifelse(
    levene_test$`Pr(>F)`[1] < 0.001,
    "< 0.001",
    paste("=", round(levene_test$`Pr(>F)`[1], 3))
  ),
  ").\n"
)

Stats: Does testing volume explain incrased in pos cases?

models_analysis <- pos_annual_prop_no_multi %>%
  filter(Year >= 2014, Year <= 2024) %>%
  summarise(
    # Model 1: Time trend only
    model_time = list(lm(positive_tests ~ Year, data = .)),
    # Model 2: Testing volume only
    model_volume = list(lm(positive_tests ~ total_tests, data = .)),
    # Model 3: Both time and volume
    model_combined = list(lm(positive_tests ~ Year + total_tests, data = .))
  )

# Extract model summaries

summary(models_analysis$model_time[[1]])

# Compare model fit
model_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Time Only", "Volume Only", "Time + Volume"),

    summary(models_analysis$model_time[[1]])$r.squared,
    summary(models_analysis$model_volume[[1]])$r.squared,
    summary(models_analysis$model_combined[[1]])$r.squared
  ),
  AIC = c(
    AIC(models_analysis$model_time[[1]]),
    AIC(models_analysis$model_volume[[1]]),
    AIC(models_analysis$model_combined[[1]])
  )
)

Decomp: testing volume vs pos rate contributions to case growth

Decomposes the observed change in positive cases into three additive components: - Volume effect: more tests at the baseline positivity rate - Rate effect: higher positivity rate applied to baseline test volume - Interaction: joint change in both

# Decompose case growth: volume effect vs rate effect vs interaction
decomp_cases <- pos_annual_prop_no_multi %>%
  arrange(Year) %>%
  mutate(
    tests_0 = first(total_tests),
    rate_0 = first(pos_prop) / 100,
    cases_0 = first(positive_tests),

    # Additive decomposition: Cases = Tests × Rate
    volume_effect = (total_tests - tests_0) * rate_0,
    rate_effect = tests_0 * (pos_prop / 100 - rate_0),
    interaction_effect = (total_tests - tests_0) * (pos_prop / 100 - rate_0),

    # Observed change
    cases_change = positive_tests - cases_0,

    # Percentage attribution (of observed case change)
    pct_volume = ifelse(
      cases_change != 0,
      volume_effect / cases_change * 100,
      NA
    ),
    pct_rate = ifelse(cases_change != 0, rate_effect / cases_change * 100, NA),
    pct_interaction = ifelse(
      cases_change != 0,
      interaction_effect / cases_change * 100,
      NA
    )
  )

cat("=== CASE GROWTH DECOMPOSITION ===\n\n")
decomp_cases %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Year,
    cases_change,
    volume_effect,
    rate_effect,
    interaction_effect,
    pct_volume,
    pct_rate,
    pct_interaction
  ) %>%
  print(n = 11)

# Summary for 2024 vs 2014 baseline
d2024 <- decomp_cases %>% filter(Year == 2024)
cat("\n=== 2024 vs 2014 BASELINE ===\n")
cat("Observed case increase:", d2024$cases_change, "\n")
cat(
  "Volume effect:",
  round(d2024$volume_effect, 1),
  "(",
  round(d2024$pct_volume, 1),
  "%)\n"
)
cat(
  "Rate effect:",
  round(d2024$rate_effect, 1),
  "(",
  round(d2024$pct_rate, 1),
  "%)\n"
)
cat(
  "Interaction:",
  round(d2024$interaction_effect, 1),
  "(",
  round(d2024$pct_interaction, 1),
  "%)\n"
)
cat(
  "Sum of components:",
  round(d2024$volume_effect + d2024$rate_effect + d2024$interaction_effect, 1),
  "\n"
)

# Visualise decomposition over time
decomp_long <- decomp_cases %>%
  filter(Year > 2014) %>%
  dplyr::select(Year, volume_effect, rate_effect, interaction_effect) %>%
  pivot_longer(-Year, names_to = "component", values_to = "cases") %>%
  mutate(
    component = factor(
      component,
      levels = c("volume_effect", "rate_effect", "interaction_effect"),
      labels = c("Testing volume", "Positivity rate", "Interaction")
    )
  )

# Stacked bar chart of absolute contributions
p_decomp_abs <- ggplot(
  decomp_long,
  aes(x = Year, y = cases, fill = component)
) +
  geom_col(alpha = 0.8, width = 0.7) +
  geom_point(
    data = decomp_cases %>% filter(Year > 2014),
    aes(x = Year, y = cases_change, fill = NULL),
    shape = 21,
    size = 2.5,
    fill = "white",
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Testing volume" = "black",
      "Positivity rate" = "grey60",
      "Interaction" = "grey85"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2015, 2024, 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.05))) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Change in positive cases\n(relative to 2014)",
    fill = "Component"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

p_decomp_abs
